title: sha2 0.10 → 0.11 in the osf crate
summary: The osf crate bumps its sha2 dependency from 0.10 to 0.11, which pulls the RustCrypto digest stack forward: digest 0.11, block-buffer 0.12, crypto-common 0.2 and cpufeatures 0.3. The old generic-array/typenum/version_check trio is dropped in favour of hybrid-array, and const-oid appears as a new transitive dependency of digest. Only the lockfile and the one version constraint in crates/osf/Cargo.toml change; no source file is touched, so the hashing call sites in osf keep their existing shape while the implementation underneath them is replaced.

nodes.label: osf crate
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf
nodes.summary: The crate whose manifest changes: its sha2 requirement moves from 0.10 to 0.11. No source file in the crate is edited, so the hashing call sites are unchanged and only the resolved implementation differs.

nodes.label: Cargo.lock
nodes.subtitle: resolved dependency graph
nodes.summary: The lockfile records the new resolution: sha2 0.11.0, digest 0.11.3, block-buffer 0.12.1, crypto-common 0.2.2, cpufeatures 0.3.1 and the new hybrid-array and const-oid entries, with generic-array and version_check removed.

nodes.label: sha2
nodes.summary: The SHA-2 implementation itself. The 0.11 release is built against digest 0.11 and cpufeatures 0.3, so its public surface and internal buffer types move with the trait generation.

nodes.label: digest
nodes.summary: The trait crate that defines the hashing interface sha2 implements. It now depends on const-oid in addition to block-buffer and crypto-common, and drops its typenum dependency.

nodes.label: crypto-common
nodes.summary: Shared traits and types for the RustCrypto crates. Its dependency on generic-array and typenum is replaced by hybrid-array.

nodes.label: block-buffer
nodes.summary: The fixed-size block buffer used by block-based hashes. It swaps generic-array for hybrid-array, which is the mechanical core of this upgrade.

nodes.label: hybrid-array
nodes.subtitle: 0.4.15 (new)
nodes.summary: Newly introduced array abstraction that replaces generic-array across the digest stack. It depends only on typenum.

nodes.label: generic-array
nodes.subtitle: 0.14.7 (gone)
nodes.summary: The previous array abstraction, no longer referenced by any crate in the graph after the upgrade.

nodes.label: const-oid
nodes.subtitle: 0.10.2 (new)
nodes.summary: New transitive dependency pulled in by digest 0.11; it was not present in the base lockfile.

nodes.label: cpufeatures
nodes.summary: Runtime CPU feature detection used by sha2 to pick accelerated backends. The 0.3 line is the version compatible with sha2 0.11.

nodes.label: libc
nodes.subtitle: platform syscalls
nodes.summary: Unchanged dependency of cpufeatures; included as context because it sits directly under the upgraded crate.

edges.label: sha2 = "0.11"
edges.summary: The single authored change in this diff: the osf crate's sha2 requirement moves from 0.10 to 0.11, which is what forces the rest of the lockfile churn.
The lockfile pins the newly resolved sha2 version and its checksum.
sha2 implements the digest traits; the 0.11 release targets digest 0.11.
sha2 uses cpufeatures to detect SHA-NI and other accelerated paths at runtime.
digest buffers input blocks through block-buffer, now at 0.12.
digest builds on the shared traits in crypto-common 0.2.
New edge in this change: digest 0.11 now depends on const-oid, which did not appear in the base lockfile.
block-buffer 0.12 is generic over hybrid-array instead of generic-array.
The old generic-array dependency of block-buffer, gone in the new resolution.
crypto-common's former generic-array dependency, also removed.
cpufeatures still reaches the platform through libc; unchanged by this diff.
